💵 "The Nasdaq just added $1 trillion!" You've probably seen it today. Here's what it really means.

📈 What happened: US shares rallied strongly on Monday. At the close, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was up 2.7%, the S&P 500 up 2.4% (its best day since April) and the Dow up 1,104 points (2.2%). Chip companies led the rebound after last week's sell-off in AI stocks. Nvidia went the other way and fell.

🤔 The "$1 trillion": that's how much the total value of the companies' shares went up during the day (some reports say $1.5 trillion for all US shares). It is NOT $1 trillion of new cash flowing into the market. If share prices fall tomorrow, that value shrinks just as quickly. It's paper value, and it can change the next day.

🇿🇦 What it means for you: many South African retirement annuities, unit trusts and tax-free savings accounts hold global shares, including big US tech companies. A day like this lifts their value; a bad week pulls it down. What counts for your savings is the long run, not one exciting day.

Education, not financial advice.
